title: Banks — Create / Edit
overviewHtml: The banks employees are paid into and the banks the organisation pays from. Each employee bank account names one of these banks, and the salary transfer file is produced for one paying bank at a time.

fields.label: Code
fields.rules: Optional. Left blank, the next number is assigned when the record is saved. Must be unique in this list.
fields.html:
What it is. A short code that identifies this item in its list.

Example. 001

fields.label: NameEn
fields.rules: Required. Must be unique in this list.
fields.html: What it is. The item's name in English.

fields.label: NameAr
fields.rules: Required. Must be unique in this list.
fields.html: What it is. The item's name in Arabic.

fields.label: ExternalCode
fields.html:
What it is. An identifier for this bank used outside HCMv3.

Why it matters. When this bank pays salaries, its external code is written into the salary transfer file.

fields.label: SWIFTCode
fields.html:
What it is. The bank's SWIFT (BIC) code.

Example. NBOKKWKW

Why it matters. Written into the salary transfer file for employees who are paid into this bank.

fields.label: CompanyCode
fields.html:
What it is. A company code for this bank, as its transfer file format requires.

Why it matters. When this bank pays salaries, this code is written into the salary transfer file.

fields.label: BankFile
fields.rules: Optional. Chosen from Bank File master data.
fields.html:
What it is. A bank file format linked to this bank.

Why it matters. Not read at present — the salary transfer file does not use this setting.
fields.adminHtml: The codes a paying bank uses for other banks in its transfer file are set in Payee Bank Details.
